item.title: Building an Internal Developer Platform with Artificial Intelligence
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/platform-artificial-intelligence/en/headerimage/platform-artificial-intellgience-header-1789459416087.jpg"/><p>Agents are becoming the new developer platform, using semantic search with data from tools like Git, Slack, and Jira for context. Things to consider are setting guardrails to block or allow things, and using logs, metrics, and traces to understand agent behavior.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

item.title: Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Project Karmada Reaches CNCF Graduation
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/karmada-kubernetes-cncf/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789562925561.jpg"/><p>The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) announced on September 2026 that Karmada, a multi-cluster and multi-cloud Kubernetes orchestration project, has graduated. This multi-cluster and multi-cloud Kubernetes orchestration project reached CNCF's highest maturity tier.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Presentation: When Incidents Refuse to End
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/stream-incidents/en/mediumimage/vanessa-huerta-medium-1789021024982.jpeg"/><p>Vanessa Huerta Granda explains how marathon incidents expose the gap between work as imagined and work as done. Drawing from real-world scenarios, she shares how complex outages reveal organizational fragility, human limits, and system interdependencies—and why incident response requires structured endurance, humane rotations, and holistic cross-functional coordination.</p> <i>By Vanessa Huerta Granda</i>

item.title: Repeated VM Escapes By GPT-5.6-Cyber Based Agents Prove VMs and OS' Require Better Maintenance
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/agent-escape-vm/en/headerimage/headerRobotEscape-1789626255584.jpg"/><p>Traditional virtual machines are inadequate for isolating cyber-capable autonomous agents. Tests using GPT-5.6-Cyber indicated multiple escape attempts due to kernel flaws. While Firecracker provided some containment, vulnerabilities remained. The study underscores the need for minimal attack surface virtualisation technologies and rapid, proactive patching strategies to safeguard host systems.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: TanStack Charts Introduced with a Framework Agnostic Grammar of Graphics for TypeScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/tanstack-charts-alpha-introduced/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789574181602.jpg"/><p>TanStack Charts is a new, framework-agnostic visualization library for TypeScript. It allows developers to create visualizations by composing various elements instead of using fixed chart types. Currently in Alpha, it has about 160,000 weekly downloads. The library supports multiple frameworks and is designed for a variety of environments, though it is not yet stable for production use.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Is the First Model OpenAI Classifies as Critical for Cybersecurity
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/gpt-6-astra-critical-cyber/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789311714190.jpg"/><p>OpenAI has classified GPT-6 Astra at the Critical cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework, a first. In expert-led testing the model found previously unknown vulnerabilities in a browser and an OS kernel and built working exploits. The same system card reports a substantial decline in chain-of-thought monitorability.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/microsoft-taugrid-open-source/en/headerimage/microsoft-phi-4-1789581142435.jpeg"/><p>Microsoft has open-sourced TauGrid, a cloud-native platform designed to manage, schedule, and monitor AI workloads on GPU-enabled Kubernetes clusters.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Dropbox Evolves Riviera Content Processing Platform to Support AI Workloads
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Dropbox has evolved Riviera from a file preview service into a universal content processing platform supporting more than 300 file formats and over 100 transformation capabilities. Processing hundreds of thousands of transformations per second, Riviera now supports Search, Replay, Sign, and Dash, while its APIs enable asynchronous content extraction for AI and RAG workflows.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Shopify Drops React Native for Swift and Kotlin as AI Changes Cross-Platform Development Tradeoffs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/shopify-drops-react-native/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789561441081.jpg"/><p>Shopify recently announced it is abandoning React Native to rewrite its flagship apps in Swift and Kotlin. With the significant jump in the quality of AI models, Head of Mobile Mustafa Ali reassessed Shopify’s commitment to React Native, estimating that the benefit/cost ratio of maintaining native codebases across mobile platforms was now above that of using an abstraction layer.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

item.title: Article: Your Next DSL Author Is a Language Model
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/next-dsl-author-language-model/en/smallimage/Your-Next-DSL-Author-Is-a-Language-Model-thumb-1789048983233.jpg"/><p>In this article, the author introduces Typed Domain Grounding, an approach to reducing LLM hallucinations in domain-specific languages by embedding them in mainstream typed languages. Using kUML benchmarks and an infrastructure-as-code example, he explores how compiler validation and generate-compile-repair loops can make model-generated DSL output more reliable.</p> <i>By Irakli Betchvaia</i>

item.title: Lyft Moves Streaming Fleet to Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/lyft-flink-k8s-operator/en/headerimage/header-1788786681315.jpeg"/><p>Lyft has moved hundreds of production Flink jobs from a 2020 in-house Kubernetes operator to the Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator, unlocking last-state upgrades, in-place autoscaling and resource autotuning across the fleet.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: Presentation: Teaching Engineers, Trusting AI: How Education Enabled Autonomous Code Review
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/duolingo-ai-literacy-code-review/en/mediumimage/sarah-deitke-medium-1788338781338.jpeg"/><p>Sarah Deitke discusses how Duolingo drives cultural AI adoption beyond tooling access. She explains their internal AI literacy workshops and observability dashboards, then shares a case study on redesigning code review using an automated PR risk-assessment bot. Deitke demonstrates how pairing targeted developer education with safe AI guardrails speeds up delivery without increasing defect rates.</p> <i>By Sarah Deitke</i>

item.title: Java 27 Delivers Post-Quantum Cryptography, Future Language Innovation, Helidon 27, JavaFX 27
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/java27-released/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1789513423942.jpg"/><p>Oracle has released version 27 of the Java programming language and virtual machine. As the second non-LTS release since JDK 25, the final feature set includes nine JEPs, five of which are still progressing through the preview and incubator stages. This release focuses on strengthening security, future language innovation, and projects under the auspices of the Java Verified Portfolio.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Dropbox Outlines How Focusing on Existing Infrastructure Efficiency Can Create Headroom for AI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/dropbox-datacenter/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789513176018.jpg"/><p>Dropbox has outlined how a decade of infrastructure optimization is helping it absorb growing demand from AI without treating new data-center capacity as the only answer. Its work spans forecasting, fleet utilization, storage density, hardware lifecycles, and rack-level power delivery, much of it predating the current AI boom.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

item.title: From Memory-Hungry HNSW to Quantized SPANN: The Technical Evolution of Pinterest's Manas Platform
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/pinterest-search/en/headerimage/HG-1789489973604.jpg"/><p>Pinterest Engineering has enhanced its Manas search platform to manage vast data, improving efficiency in search and discovery functions. By applying Scalar and Product Quantization, memory usage decreased significantly while maintaining high recall rates. The platform utilizes SSDs for optimized performance, and it is transitioning to multi-vector models for refined relevance matching.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: AI-Assisted Discovery Helps Microsoft Patch More Than 1,000 Vulnerabilities in a Month
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/microsoft-ai-security-patch/en/headerimage/microsoft-llm-contextual-privacy-1789488709548.jpeg"/><p>With its latest September 2026 Patch, which addresses more than 950 vulnerabilities, Microsoft has patched about 2,750 vulnerabilities so far this year. While many attribute this surge to AI-assisted security research, organizations may struggle to keep pace and fully benefit from these advances, particularly when it comes to evaluating, prioritizing, and deploying patches.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Atlassian Automates Root Cause Analysis by Correlating Metrics, Logs and Traces
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/atlassian-automated-rca/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789026479583.jpg"/><p>Atlassian has outlined a new approach to automating root cause analysis for large-scale cloud-native incidents, using correlation across metrics, logs, distributed traces, and service topology to generate ranked hypotheses about where failures originate and how they propagate.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Amazon Linux 2027 Enters Public Preview with SELinux Enforcing by Default
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/amazon-linux-2027-preview/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789307005573.jpg"/><p>AWS has released Amazon Linux 2027 in public preview, built on the AL2023 baseline with kernel 7.1 and SELinux in enforcing mode by default. Applications that pass on AL2023's permissive mode may fail under enforcing. The announcement gives no AL2023 end-of-support date, no GA date, and no in-place migration path.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Agoda Replaces 72-Shard SQL Server Price Cache with DragonflyDB
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/agoda-price-cache-dragonflydb/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787939534250.jpg"/><p>Agoda migrated its 1.5 TB hotel Price Cache from 72 SQL Server shards to DragonflyDB to handle growing read and write volumes. The migration used staged dual reads, parity validation, gradual traffic shifting, and decentralized failover detection. Agoda reports an approximately eightfold reduction in P99 read latency, with two DragonflyDB clusters providing high availability.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Jotai 3.0 Ships as a Modernized, ESM-Only Package That Drops Legacy Builds and Deprecated APIs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/jotai-3-released/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789141759444.jpg"/><p>Jotai, an atomic state management library for React, has released version 3.0.0, now exclusively using ES modules. It maintains backward compatibility but removes some deprecated APIs. Migration is straightforward for most users. This version emphasizes a leaner core with improvements while deferring significant feature changes for future updates.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Meta Open-Sources Astryx, its Agent-Ready React Design System
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/meta-astryx-design-system/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789341796965.jpg"/><p>Meta recently announced the beta release of Astryx, an open-source React design system developed internally over eight years. Astryx builds on React 19 and StyleX to provide over 150 accessible UI components, customizable CSS design tokens, and dedicated CLI and MCP tooling — for both engineers and AI agents.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

item.title: Lambda SnapStart Comes to Container Images, Ending a Packaging Tradeoff
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/lambda-snapstart-container-image/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789052932475.jpg"/><p>AWS has extended Lambda SnapStart to container image functions, which hold up to 10 GB against 250 MB for zip archives. Teams previously chose between dependency headroom and sub-second startup. A Reddit thread from a month earlier shows what that cost: stripping whitespace and docstrings from installed packages to stay under the limit.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Netflix Reworks Conductor for 420 Million Monthly Workflow Executions and 10X Larger Workflows
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/netflix-conductor-4-workflow/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787938102526.jpg"/><p>Netflix has reworked its Conductor workflow orchestration engine to handle larger workloads, increasing supported workflow size from about 2,500 to 30,000 tasks and reducing p99 workflow evaluation latency by about 40%. Conductor 4.0 separates workflow metadata from task data, moves evaluation to asynchronous processing, and introduces dynamic worker allocation and concurrency controls.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: tsgolint Reaches Stable v7, Bringing Go-Powered Type-Aware Linting to Oxlint
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/tsgolint-oxlint-typescript/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789113850089.jpg"/><p>tsgolint has released a stable v7, enhancing TypeScript linting with native Go speed. It offers type-aware linting, leveraging TypeScript's semantic analysis through the typescript-go compiler. Oxlint manages configurations and file discovery. The release, compatible with TypeScript 7.0.2, handles 59 of 61 type-aware rules and shows significant performance improvements over ESLint.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Terraform AWS Provider Continues Rapid Expansion as AWS Infrastructure Becomes More Complex
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/terraform-aws-provider-6-62/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788446872951.jpg"/><p>The Terraform AWS Provider continues its rapid evolution, with v6.62.0 adding support for new AWS capabilities while improving how Terraform understands and manages existing infrastructure.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: How to Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not to
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/form3-multicloud-architecture/en/mediumimage/ross-mcfarlane-kevin-holditch-medium-1788338652847.jpg"/><p>Ross McFarlane and Kevin Holditch discuss Form3's evolution from a single-cloud setup to a triple active multi-cloud architecture. They share key engineering strategies for cross-cloud networking, distributed databases with CockroachDB and NATS, custom Kubernetes operators, and navigating distinct regional disaster recovery expectations across the UK, Europe, and US financial markets.</p> <i>By Ross McFarlane, Kevin Holditch</i>

item.title: vlt 1.0 Ships as a Drop-in npm Replacement with Phased Installs, Graph Queries, and Malware-Blocking
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788539629791.jpg"/><p>vlt, created by the original npm team, has launched version 1.0 as a drop-in replacement for npm. It features phased installations to prevent automatic script execution, a queryable dependency graph with over 60 selectors, and hosted registries that block malicious packages. The tool aims to enhance security and streamline the JavaScript development process.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Blume: Zero-Config Docs Framework That Turns a Markdown Folder into an AI-Ready Website
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/blume-docs-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788535805507.jpg"/><p>Blume is an open-source documentation framework that converts Markdown into a complete documentation site. Built with Astro and Vite, it requires only Node.js and a single Markdown file for setup. The framework supports various configurations, offers automatic SEO features, and includes tools for document testing. It facilitates migration from other documentation systems.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Twenty Years of jQuery: How a Little Library Rewired Web Development
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/jquery-20-years/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788335247571.jpg"/><p>jQuery, created by John Resig and released in 2006, is a JavaScript library that simplifies HTML manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax. It enabled easier web development by providing an accessible API across browsers. While its use has declined with the rise of modern frameworks, jQuery remains prevalent on a significant portion of websites today.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
